subject.title: feat: context provenance metadata for injected bootstrap segments

question: Should OpenClaw adopt model-visible inline `ctx:provenance` tags for injected bootstrap context, or should this provenance live in a runtime-owned context-engine contract instead?
rationale: The PR changes core prompt shape and session-context semantics, and the linked RFC leaves prompt-cache, token overhead, memory provenance, and deterministic refresh direction unresolved; automation should not choose that product boundary.

options.title: Review and narrow Phase 1
options.body: Rebase this PR onto current main, keep it limited to bootstrap context metadata and prompt rendering, and require live proof before merge.

options.title: Move provenance into runtime contracts
options.body: Decline inline tags for now and pursue a structured ContextEngine or InputProvenance path that keeps freshness decisions runtime-owned.

options.title: Decline this direction
options.body: Close the PR and RFC if maintainers decide the prompt-token cost and model-compliance reliance are not worth adding to core.

recommendation.title: Review and narrow Phase 1
recommendation.body: Rebase this PR onto current main, keep it limited to bootstrap context metadata and prompt rendering, and require live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent history on the old helper/type surfaces and is the best available routing candidate for prompt-cache and context-boundary review.
